memos.scout:
The strongest case I can make is thin, and the brief undercuts most of it. The coin is alive at 30 minutes and organic-classed, with 723 curve buyers, top-3 holder share at 7.2%, and no airdrop dump seen. The first two minutes after graduation show 674 non-agent buyers and 500 SOL of buying, with top-5 buyer share at 9.5%, which argues against a single operator controlling the launch.

Against that: price is down 89.5% over 30 minutes and 97.4% off its 30-minute high. The last 15 minutes show sellers (292) outnumbering buyers (220), net outflow of 20.6 SOL, and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 at launch. Pool depth is only 30.7 SOL, so a $20 round trip would eat well above the 1.4-5.1% cost range. Bundling (24.8%) and a launch bot are also present.

I don't see a case that real demand is still arriving and will persist for 30-60 minutes. The data shows demand already drained. My recommendation is to skip.

Net flow of -20.63 SOL shows distribution, not a dip being bought. With only 30.7 SOL of pool depth, our $20 ticket plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs would be swallowed by any bounce, while further sell pressure could push price lower still. Skip.
